description: Asteroid Avengers participates in the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Our mission is to breathe digital life into silent rovers and landers on the Moon and Mars using an interactive AI platform.We combine NASA open data with modern software engineering and AI models to build comprehensive storytelling software, giving these historical machines a voice to share their cosmic journey and legacy.
summary:
Millions of kilometers away on the Moon and Mars, dozens of historic NASA machines sit in silence. From the Apollo 15, 16, and 17 Lunar Roving Vehicles to Mars rovers like Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance, these explorers changed what we know about our solar system—yet their stories often stay hidden inside dense technical archives.

Team Asteroid Avengers built "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" to give these silent machines a voice. Our interactive platform maps where each rover and lunar vehicle rests today, pairing real NASA coordinates and mission timelines with simple, human storytelling. Students and space enthusiasts can click any pinned explorer, compare how long it was planned to last versus how long it actually survived, and experience the journey behind every discovery.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

"Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" is an interactive storytelling and space telemetry platform built for students, teachers, and anyone curious about space exploration. When users open the platform, they can choose between the Moon and Mars, click on pinned landing and final resting sites, and explore the real journeys of NASA's left-behind hardware—including the Apollo 15–17 Lunar Roving Vehicles, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance.

Each explorer card breaks down complex mission logs into clear, relatable stories: where it landed, what problems it solved, how far it traveled, and how long it survived against the odds (such as Opportunity working for nearly 15 years instead of its planned 90 Martian days).

Why We Built It & Intended Impact:

Most space data is published in raw scientific formats that feel intimidating to young learners. Our goal was to turn real telemetry into an engaging visual journey that sparks STEM curiosity—especially for students in developing regions—while preserving the human courage and engineering behind each mission.

Tools & Technologies Used:

- Frontend & Interface: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript.

- Backend & Data Structuring: Python and Node.js to organize NASA mission coordinates, sol counts, and travel distances into clean JSON datasets.

- Multimedia Storytelling: A 240-second narrated documentary video and visual mission cards created by our team.

Design Considerations:

We prioritized fast loading, mobile-friendly navigation, and zero login barriers so anyone can explore the stories immediately.
